## Problem
How do I extract a variable from an ICESat-2 along-track data set using NASA Harmony services via the harmony-py Python library?

## Solution


```python
from harmony import BBox, Client, Collection, Request
import datetime as dt
```

Initialize your Harmony client.
```python 
harmony_client = Client()
```

Define which data set you'd like to access using the collection concept-id (see [how-to](/how-to-guides/get_concept_ids.qmd) for retrieving collection concept-ids). For this example, we'll use ATLAS/ICESat-2 L3A Along Track Coastal and Nearshore Bathymetry (ATL24 version 003) = C4312123631-NSIDC_CPRD.
```python
collection = Collection(id='C4312123631-NSIDC_CPRD') 
```

Define your spatial area of interest (here - north coast of Madagascar).
```python
bbox = BBox(48.3,-13.6,49.1,-11.8)
```
Define your temporal range.
```python
temporal = {'start': dt.datetime(2018, 12, 28),'stop': dt.datetime(2018, 12, 29)}
```
Define your variables of interest.  We'll retrieve the orthometric height of the photon (ortho_h), the photon classification (class_ph), and the classification confidence (confidence).  We specify the variable paths within the hdf5 file.
```python
variables = ['gt2l/ortho_h','gt2l/class_ph','gt2l/confidence']
```

Build the request and verify it's valid.
```python
request = Request(
    collection = collection,
    spatial = bbox,
    temporal = temporal,
    variables = variables
)
request.is_valid()
```
Submit the request.  This returns a Harmony job ID that can be used to check on progress.
```python
job_id = harmony_client.submit(request)
job_id
```
'4f37e34d-ff8e-4867-bded-9ef94b652fe7'

You can check on Harmony job progress.
```python
harmony_client.wait_for_processing(job_id, show_progress=True)
```
 [ Processing: 100% ] |###################################################| [|]

View a summary of the Harmony job. 
```python
job_summary = harmony_client.result_json(job_id)
job_summary
```

Notice the last three items in the json response.  The original data volume was 490.53 MiB and the subsetted data is 17.47 MiB.

Download the results to your local directory
```python
futures = harmony_client.download_all(job_id, directory=".", overwrite=False)
filelist = [f.result() for f in futures]  # get filepaths
len(filelist)
```

## Discussion
NASA Harmony is comprised of cloud-based services that allow you to customize many NASA data sets, providing the ability to subset, reproject and reformat files. Not all transformation services are available for all datasets.
[Table](https://nsidc.org/data/user-resources/help-center/what-subsetting-and-reformatting-services-are-available-icesat-2-data) of Harmony services available for select ICESat-2 data sets.

A longer form tutorial demonstrating NASA Harmony and the harmony-py Python library can be found [here](https://nasa-openscapes.github.io/earthdata-cloud-cookbook/tutorials/Harmony.html).
